meta.description: Download genome assemblies, gene records, and ortholog data from NCBI using the modern Datasets v2 CLI (replaces assembly_summary.txt scraping and many EFetch workflows). Use when bulk-pulling genome assemblies, gene metadata across species, ortholog sets, or BLAST databases; when E-utilities are too slow for genome-scale work; or when automatic checksum verification, parallel download, and clean accession-driven retrieval are required.

scientific_integrity.detail: All values returned across all 7 inputs (organism names, lengths, gene IDs, ortholog counts) traced to real, live NCBI Datasets API responses; no fabricated accessions, counts, or metadata observed.

practice_boundaries.detail: Not applicable in practice — this Skill retrieves public genome/gene database records, no diagnostic, prescriptive, or patient-level content is produced or possible via this CLI.

methodological_ground.detail: No statistical or causal claims are made; the ortholog-set caveat (one representative per species, not tree-reconciled orthology) is stated accurately in both SKILL.md and usage-guide.md.

code_usability.detail: The datasets/dataformat CLI itself runs correctly throughout; several of the Skill's own shipped code patterns and example scripts fail unmodified against the installed CLI (18.37.0) due to flag/field renames (Inputs 1, 2, 3, 4) — scored down heavily in Code Executability and Correctness rather than vetoed, consistent with how equivalent API-drift breakage was handled in sibling Skills in this same folder (entrez-fetch, entrez-link, local-blast) — none of which crossed into infinite loops, injection risk, or complete non-functionality of the underlying tool.

functional_suitability.note: Covers genome/gene/ortholog/virus/dehydrate-rehydrate workflows as promised, but Correctness is weak: nearly every dataformat --fields example and the entire 'gene metadata across species' pattern fail on the installed CLI (18.37.0) exactly as written.

reliability.note: A nonexistent-but-well-formed accession returns exit 0 with {"total_count": 0} and no not-found signal (undocumented); bulk_dehydrated.sh's aria2c transform corrupts every downloaded filename silently, with no error at any point.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is concise (~300 lines) with usage-guide.md and examples/ carrying the depth; dehydrated-first guidance for bulk pulls is genuinely efficient and was confirmed to avoid a scope-explosion pull.

agent_usability.note: Clear Datasets-vs-E-utilities decision table and subcommand taxonomy, but an agent following the doc's own code patterns hits four distinct live failures (taxon-level gene query, two field-name sets, bare --ortholog) that the Failure Modes/Common Errors sections do not cover.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language in the description; CLI error messages are mostly clear and actionable except the silent zero-count case and the misleading --ortholog error.

security.note: Example scripts consistently quote shell variables; no hardcoded secrets; --api-key is documented only as an inline CLI argument with no env-var alternative suggested.

maintainability.note: Clean modular layering (SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / 3 single-purpose example scripts); Testability is low because none of the 3 shipped example scripts currently runs unmodified against the pinned CLI version.

agent_specific.note: Precise, well-scoped trigger description; strong Related-Skills composability and escape-hatch table — independently verified true (datasets download has no SRA subcommand at all), not just asserted.

key_strengths: Live, biologically correct results across every core workflow once corrected for current-CLI syntax: accurate phiX174 assembly stats, a real 558-record BRCA1 ortholog set, and a real 273-genome bulk Deinococcus pull.
Scope discipline is not just documented but verifiably true — the CLI genuinely has no SRA-read subcommand, confirming the Skill's own decision table routes correctly to sra-data.
The dehydrate-then-rehydrate design (with automatic MD5 verification) worked flawlessly end to end at both single-accession and 273-genome scale via datasets rehydrate.

Clean progressive disclosure across SKILL.md, usage-guide.md, and three single-purpose example scripts, with a Version Compatibility section that correctly anticipates the exact class of CLI drift that broke its own examples.

recommendations.title: 'Gene metadata across species' pattern does not work as documented
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's code pattern and examples/gene_metadata.sh's own default (TAXON=Mammalia) call `datasets summary gene symbol BRCA1 --taxon Mammalia`, which fails outright: 'gene requires an at-or-below-species-level taxon.' There is no supported way to get multi-species gene records via this subcommand.
recommendations.root_cause: The doc treats --taxon on `summary gene symbol` as a clade-level filter, but the flag's real contract (confirmed via live --help and the error text) is single-species only; the only true multi-species mechanism is the separate --ortholog flag, which returns a materially narrower result (one representative per species).
recommendations.fix: Rewrite 'Gene metadata across species' to either loop --taxon <species> per species of interest, or point at --ortholog all and remove the false claim that --taxon <clade> performs a cross-species query. Change gene_metadata.sh's default TAXON to a real species.

recommendations.title: dataformat --fields names are stale across every shipped code block
recommendations.problem: `dataformat tsv genome --fields assembly-level,scaffold-n50,contig-n50,total-sequence-length` and `dataformat tsv gene --fields taxname,nomenclature-authority-symbol` both error 'field(s) [...] not recognized' on the installed CLI (18.37.0).
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md is pinned to '16.0+ (2024)'; the field-name catalog was renamed by 18.37.0 and none of the doc's own dataformat calls were re-verified against a current --help catalog.
recommendations.fix: Update every --fields list to: assminfo-level, assmstats-scaffold-n50, assmstats-contig-n50, assmstats-total-sequence-len, tax-name. Drop nomenclature-authority-symbol entirely; no replacement field exists.

recommendations.title: bulk_dehydrated.sh silently corrupts every downloaded filename
recommendations.problem: fetch.txt is 3 tab-separated columns (<url>, a '0' placeholder, <path>) on the installed CLI, not the 2 columns the script's comment and its awk line (line 31) assume. Running it unmodified writes 'out=0' for every queued file, with no error at any point — confirmed at both 1-file and 273-file scale.
recommendations.root_cause: fetch.txt's schema gained a byte-size-placeholder middle column since the script was last verified against a live CLI version.
recommendations.fix: Change line 31 to `awk -F'\t' '{print $1"\n  out="$3}'` (third field, not second), and add a sanity check that fails loudly if any generated 'out=' line reads 'out=0'.

recommendations.title: --ortholog bare-flag syntax is broken with a misleading error
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's 'Find orthologs for a gene' pattern and usage-guide.md's ortholog example call `--ortholog --as-json-lines` (bare flag). On 18.37.0 this makes the CLI consume '--as-json-lines' as --ortholog's argument, then fail trying to resolve it as a taxon name, printing 10 unrelated taxonomic suggestions with no indication the real problem is a missing flag value.
recommendations.root_cause: --ortholog changed from a boolean flag to `--ortholog strings` between CLI major versions; the doc's Version Compatibility section anticipates this class of drift abstractly but its own examples were not re-verified.
recommendations.fix: Change every --ortholog invocation in SKILL.md and usage-guide.md to `--ortholog all` (or an explicit taxon list).

recommendations.title: Nonexistent accessions fail silently, undocumented
recommendations.problem: `datasets summary genome accession GCF_999999999.1` exits 0 and prints `{"total_count": 0}` with no 'not found' message; an agent or script checking exit code alone would treat this as success.
recommendations.root_cause: Not covered by SKILL.md's 'Common errors' table, which lists 7 other rows but not this response shape.
recommendations.fix: Add a Common errors row: '{"total_count": 0}, exit 0 -> accession doesn't exist, was withdrawn, or was superseded; verify at ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets.'

recommendations.title: 'dataformat version' prints the literal string 'undefined'
recommendations.problem: `dataformat.exe version` exits 0 with stdout exactly 'undefined', despite --help describing it as printing the client version. datasets --version works correctly.
recommendations.root_cause: Version-reporting is unimplemented for dataformat specifically in this CLI build.
recommendations.fix: Note this defect explicitly in the Version Compatibility section; tell the agent to confirm the dataformat build via its --help banner or by checking it shipped alongside a known-good datasets binary, not via dataformat version.
